title: SLO partnership sprintkit and crossfunctional radar
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic 90-day sprintkit for operationalizing SLO ownership across product, serving runtime, and platform teams. Focus is on a small set of cross-functional deliverables that reduce blast radius and enable predictable launches for model-serving features.

High-level goals (90d):
- Get 3 pilot services to a common SLO definition and automated validation pipeline.
- Ship an Error Budget Policy template and two automated enforcement hooks (alerting + routing fallback).
- Reduce P95 latency variance on model-serving by 20% for pilot cohort via batching/caching experiments.

Who: (RACI snapshot)
- R: Emma Chen (SRE lead), Asha Patel (Platform eng owner)
- A: Luca Moretti (Product PM), Priya Singh (Serving runtime eng)
- C: Solutions eng, Support triage, Observability
- I: Head of Eng, Customer Success for pilot customers

Core deliverables:
1) SLO Definition Kit: short template (SLO target, measurement window, user-impact mapping, allowable error types). One-page canonical doc + example for chat-generation and embedding endpoints.
2) SLO-as-code validators: lightweight CI check that rejects PRs lacking SLO metadata. Integrates with github PR comment bot.
3) Error Budget Policy + Enforcement: pager thresholds, auto-fallback routing policy (route to cheaper model variant or degraded feature), and postmortem trigger.
4) Observability Dashboard Tile: per-route unit cost, token latency percentiles, and error budget burn rate.
5) Experiment pack: A/B test recipe for batching and prefix caching with measurement checklist.

Quartered milestones (weeks):
- Week 0-2: kickoff workshop (RACI, scope pilot services). Kickoff artifacts: SLO templates + initial metrics queries.
- Week 3-6: Implement SLO-as-code + validate against pilot services. Build dashboard tile prototype.
- Week 7-10: Run batching/caching experiments; iterate on autoscaling thresholds.
- Week 11-12: Lock error budget policy; enable auto-routing fallback for pilot; conduct tabletop run.

Risk & mitigations:
- Measurement drift (high) — mitigation: add synthetic traffic probes and drift-alert pipeline.
- Blast radius from auto-routing — mitigation: start with canary percent and manual approval flag.
- Cross-team bandwidth mismatch — mitigation: limit scope to 3 pilot services; weekly sync and async decision log.

Communication rhythm:
- Weekly 30-minute sync (Mon 9:30 PT) with action items.
- Bi-weekly playbook review with product & solutions eng.
- Slack channel #slo-pilot (read-only cadence summary posted by bot).

Operational notes / quick wins:
- Tag metrics with route, model-variant, and customer-tier (important for differential SLOs).
- Add a small synthetic request every 5s per region to stabilize percentile calculation.
- Use error-budget burn alerts to trigger low-cost mitigations (throttle background jobs, reduce burst capacity).

Metrics to track (per-service):
- SLO compliance (30d rolling), error budget burn rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, per-token cost, invocation success rate.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Which team will own the SLO reviewers rotation? (proposal: rotating SRE + product SME, 2-week cadence)
- How aggressive do we make automatic fallback (10% -> 50% rollout path)?

Next steps (this week):
- Emma: schedule kickoff + invite pilot service owners.
- Asha: wire up dashboard skeleton and share metrics queries.
- Priya: prototype SLO-as-code validator and open repo PR.
- Luca: confirm list of pilot services and customer scenarios.

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- Keep the SLO definition minimal: user-visible availability and latency buckets only. Avoid coupling to internal infra signals.
- Ask support for 2 customer impact examples per pilot service.
- Consider a short post-launch survey to validate user impact mapping.

Appendix (links kept in artifacts):
- Example SLO template: service, SLI query, target, window, error budget action.
- Quick runbook: what to do at 25%, 50%, 80% burn.

Document history: initial draft 2026-02-15 by Emma Chen; updated with experiment notes 2026-03-02.
